utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to say good morning, for some of you good morning again. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to call its next witness? Yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But in view of the condition of health of my colleague who couldn't speak, I will take on upon myself a part of her work, if I am allowed to do so by her and Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are allowed to do so, but with her I cannot tell you. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. I have given some thought to some of the problems that we have had over the last few days with interventions by myself in relation to 65 ter summaries. And might I put forward a proposal that might ultimately overcome some of the difficulties which the Prosecution and Defence and the Trial Chamber have had in that regard. Might I do that, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Part of the problems stem from the fact that the 65 ter summaries are not contained -- firstly, are not contained in one document; and secondly, come to us in French and in a number of different letters. If I could give an example --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I interrupt, Mr. Ierace? Mr. President, I insist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't have a transcript. Later on we need to have the exact words of Mr. Ierace. I will not be able to do so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand you as -- yes, that you would interrupt Mr. Ierace. I was at the same time dealing with my transcript as well. So Mr. Ierace, this is a matter of order rather than an order of argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have the same problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can ask the parties, it is not always clear to me whether the request to interrupt deals with practical matters or with matters of argument. So would you please indicate if this would happen again, if you say, we have a practical problem with our LiveNote, then it becomes clear to me that it is not an interruption of the argument, but it's an interruption for technical reasons which of course I will always accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will be glad to do so. I don't think that the Defence has ever interrupted or at least very rarely has it interrupted the opposing party for reasons of argument. But now we have a problem, and if there are precise problems that we need to address, we need to have it on the transcript. And mine isn't working nor is the one to the left or to the right of me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a matter of fact there is a transcript, but it is not on your laptop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is exactly what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we just -- could I just perhaps take some time anyhow for everyone. Yes -- no, I am going to teach the parties how to do it themselves. If the parties would push the button at the right top corner, the cross, so that they get out of LiveNote, yes? One moment, please. So, leave LiveNote as a whole. Do you now have the general -- okay, now you take left down bottom, programmes, start. You go up to programmes, you see on the right-hand side, you see LiveNote. Go to LiveNote. Then you find LiveNote to the right of it as well. Double click on that. Yes? We are all there? Okay, then we will click on that. So now LiveNote opens; is that correct? If you are in the beginning of Windows, you put "start" and then "programmes", and then you go to the programme that is called LiveNote, yes? Then you -- if you are on LiveNote, I think there is -- you find on the right-hand side again, LiveNote. Yes? Are you on LiveNote? If you are on LiveNote, does it appear on the right-hand side as well? Does it with you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin? If you double click on LiveNote, what happens? What should happen, as a matter of fact, is that LiveNote programme appears --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have obtained the LiveNote, as far as the Defence is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will just see whether the Prosecution -- could you please assist at the other side and to see that we come to the point where LiveNote opens as a programme. And if you wait just for a second, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. So, please don't fix the problem, but just go to the point where LiveNote opens. Yes? I don't hear you. Could you please put the microphone on, please. TECHNICAL ASSISTANT: That one is a special case now it will be ready after the break, but he can use it to see the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, but what I wonder, as a matter of fact, is that the parties can solve the problems themselves just as I did. I had the same problem this morning. So you open LiveNote, and then you go to -- I think it is -- what do you have -- you have LiveNote now on your screen, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I hope so. I mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you can open the case. You now can open the case which is Galic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, but it is okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Every is working? It is connected as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Everything is okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If during the next break -- that system is different? TECHNICAL ASSISTANT: It is just a new one. It's not connected yet. Just we didn't get the last night and we couldn't find time -- that is a special one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please teach the Prosecution during the next break how to make sure that they are connected, even if something goes wrong. Go out of the programme, start it all up again, and then you can continue. Yes. That saves us, I hope, a lot of time in the future. Mr. Ierace, you were addressing the Court when we were interrupted by the technical problems. Please proceed. The transcript is running. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, even if your laptop doesn't work, then of course the LiveNote is on your main screen. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the problems which the Prosecution has encountered with the 65 ter summaries, and they seem -- and I should add that the 65 ter summaries contribute in a substantial way to our interventions, it seems to come down to two or three aspects. Firstly, there are -- the 65 ter summaries are often contained in two or three documents, the one filed in August, various letters since then. To give as an example, the witness to be called after the one about to be called was the subject of a letter which apparently contains further 65 ter information that the Defence faxed to the Prosecution last night and which, therefore, we received this morning in French. I am not complaining at all about the use of the French language. I simply make the point that we have to have it translated. So there are two of the problems. The third problem is that when one considers the evidence which is in fact given by the witnesses, not only does the witness -- do the witnesses frequently refer to significant matters which aren't in any of the summaries, but also they quite often give evidence which bears little relationship to the matters which are in the 65 ter summaries. So I have this proposal: Firstly, that when the Defence provides us with additional 65 ter material, that at the same time, they incorporate all of the material which the witness will give evidence about. I suspect that what happens is that, for whatever reason, when the Defence interview the witnesses closer to the time of their testimony, much of what was contained in the earlier 65 ter summary is no longer, for whatever reason, determined to be the subject of their evidence. To give a simple example of that, in relation to the witness we heard yesterday, the 65 ter summary referred to the witness being at a hospital that we have heard nothing about at all. So at least if the 65 ter summaries are updated, then as we receive the latest version, we know we have in one document all of the relevant material and we can better focus our preparation rather than wasting time preparing subjects which ultimately aren't the subject of testimony. That's my first suggestion, updated 65 ter summaries. Secondly, before each witness commences, it would be helpful if the Defence could simply refer to the various letters and filings which contain the 65 ter summaries for that witness, so at least we can make sure that we have in French or in English the relevant documentation. Thirdly, I will refrain, as a general rule, from rising to my feet during the course of the witness's testimony, if the witness gives evidence which is of a significant nature which is not contained in the 65 ter material. At the end of the evidence in chief, customarily, Mr. President, your wording when you ask the Prosecution to cross-examine, is, "Is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine?" If we hear fresh material or material falling from the lips of the witness of which we have had late notice and we haven't had a sufficient opportunity to prepare our cross-examination, we will say that. And if needs be, seek an adjournment or for the witness to be recalled for further cross-examination. At the conclusion of the -- either at the conclusion of the evidence in chief or at the conclusion of the witness's testimony as a whole, at that stage, with your leave, I would rise to my feet and point out what significant matters in the evidence of the witness that we have actually heard, were not indicated to us in the 65 ter summaries, and perhaps also what was in there that we didn't hear from. The reason I would do that is, we would then have on the record the situation from the Prosecution perspective, and therefore, the Prosecution would be protected in terms of any appeal point or indeed in relation to any further argument later in the trial. I make this proposal not to be argumentative, but rather to avoid, ultimately, interventions during the testimony of the witnesses, but at the same time, address the various aspects of this issue which are involved. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I also have some suggestions and some responses. My first suggestion would be, if Mr. Ierace could be briefer in his interventions, we would gain a lot of time. Secondly, it is impossible to bring things up to date. And the reason, we are wasting time. The other day a totally unfounded intervention by the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we are not going to discuss the past. You said you would like to make suggestions, and you would like to respond to the suggestions. We are not going over the same ground again. So please make suggestions, please respond to the suggestions, but don't come back to -- and I would invite the parties not to spend time on telling this Chamber how the other party wasted time. The Chamber is at every single occasion fully aware of who wastes time. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you. What I want to say, and I think I am entitled to say it, when we have frequent interventions, which seem to us to be hardly founded, we are wasting time. And in two hours, we cannot cover certain points, and we are sacrificing certain questions. If we had the time to cover everything without being interrupted, everything indicated would have been covered. That is what I wanted to point out. Another point is that Mr. Ierace seems to complain of this fact. And I wish to recall that on the part of the Prosecution case, there were many cases when we received statements of dozens of pages -- I am referring for instance to Mr. Abdul Razek --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think it was clear enough. I allowed you to make suggestions and respond to suggestions, and I said to you that I did not want at this moment want to go over ground again of the past. Would you please follow this instruction. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Mr. President, I have to confer with my client.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning the question of letters, Mr. President -- I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning the question of letters, Mr. President, that can easily be explained in order to be as effective as possible. Every time that witnesses come here to The Hague, they are submitted to cross-examination by my colleague and myself. Frequently, we discover new elements for Ms. Pilipovic who usually conducted the examination-in-chief, and also for me who interviews the witnesses for the first time. When we discover those elements, we immediately communicate them to the Prosecution and that explains why there are several letters. So surely that is not a difficult -- is such a difficulty that the Prosecution should ask of us to do whatever. We are just specifying things. However, there are cases when witnesses tell us in the courtroom, for example, last time war gas that was used that we had no idea of. And this was new, not just for the Prosecution, it was a discovery for us too. And this was a fact that we didn't know before the testimony of those witnesses. Consequently, it seems to us that not only are we acting properly with the provisions quoted by Mr. Ierace, but what is more, we have systematized our positions. We have said that for all military witnesses, all these questions can be put to the witness of course within one zone or several zones that the witness may be familiar with. So there is a general stage which is a repetitive pattern and then a more specific part. I don't think we can do more than that. So the suggestion of Mr. Ierace appears to us not to be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did hear a response to the suggestions. Are there any suggestions you would like to make yourself, as you indicated?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, my formulation was that we shouldn't waste time with such long interventions, but I don't wish to repeat myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... your suggestion. I hear the clear answer on the first proposal, the first suggestion of the Prosecution that the update would be a consolidated update, if I understand you well. The answer is that the Defence says we cannot do that. The second one was whether you could indicate at the beginning of the examination-in-chief the sources in which the Prosecution could find the elements of the summaries if they are not contained in one document. Is the Defence willing to indicate the sources? That would mean 65 ter can be found in this document, that document, that document, that document. That would take I think approximately 30 seconds for each witness. Are you -- is the Defence willing to give the sources at the beginning of the testimony in chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I would answer with "no" to that question. I will tell you why. I will explain why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please explain to us why.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because if we make a mistake or admit a document, we will be told "you did not fulfill your duty." So we write our letters and let the Prosecution read them carefully, understand them and everything will be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider the matter. The third suggestion made by Mr. Ierace I think is not in need of any response because he suggests how the Prosecution will submit their 65 ter complaints at a concentrated moment. Then, are you ready to call your next witness? Is the Defence ready? Yes. Before doing so, I can orally give you as the decision of the Chamber that the protective measures sought are granted. I will not at this moment mention the name of the witness, but I will do that in closed session and then repeat our decision. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text will be handed out to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. Since protective measures have been granted in respect of you, I will not use your name, as you will understand. Apart from not mentioning your name, your face will not be visible for the outside world. Ms. Pilipovic -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, are you ready to examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, willingly, Mr. President. As usual, we are going to start in private session? Are we in private session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we are not at this moment. What we usually do is to first present the pseudonym sheet to the witness and then turn into private session once this matter has been -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, gladly. This will be Exhibit 1784, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Piletta-Zanin:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I would appreciate it if you could just answer my answers by saying yes or no -- if you could answer my first question by saying yes or no, after I have said good day to you. The information you have on the page in front of you, is it correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we can take this document back. Are we in private session, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned the Territorial Defence. Could you tell us how this defence organised -- this defence organisation organised itself at the beginning of the events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Before the war broke out, every local commune had men in addition to the reserve police force throughout the former Yugoslavia, and they had people who were responsible for certain things. They were deployed in the civilian protection, they did the same sort of work as the men in the JNA, but within the framework of the civilian protection organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From when did this Territorial Defence organise itself, from which date did it organise itself in a military sense? Is there a particular event that you could mention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: From the time the first barracks were put up in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did this happen, as far as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I think it was in March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, as far as the repetitiousness of the evidence is concerned, is the moment the barricades were created, is that in contest, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There is no particular significance with attaches to it, Mr. President, if I can put it that way. The Prosecution accepts that barricades were erected leading up to the 6th of April, and that obviously would cover March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think we heard about the barricades, approximately 25 or 30 times, if not 40. The Chamber has to take care that evidence is not repetitious. It seems to be not in contest, so would you please move to your next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Barricades is not the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not saying that that is the problem, but you are asking the witness about barricades and when it was. I mean, if there is any other subject, please, move to that. Come to your point, but this is evidence that is repeatedly given to this Chamber. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Chronology is the problem and I am going to turn to it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to summarise your testimony in chronological terms. You said that the Territorial Defence organised itself in military terms after the barricades had been put up; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you describe the situation to us before these barricades were put up, in a few words, and I am talking about the military organisation, was there such an organisation, yes or no, before the barricades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. To the extent that this is possible, could you speak a little more loudly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, matters are clear now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you now concentrate on the period during which the JNA had to leave Bosnia, and to be more specific, had to leave Sarajevo. Do you know when this happened; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the month when the JNA withdrew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I think it was at the beginning of May, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We are now going to concentrate on the period of May. Do you know, Witness, what happened to the barracks, and not just to the barracks, but what was contained within the barracks when the army withdrew; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know it for both sides of the line; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Not fully, as far as the other side of the line is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you know what happened in a barracks called Viktor Bubanj? I think it is called Viktor Bubanj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to these barracks, do you know what happened with the equipment and the weapons when had so-called JNA Army withdrew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you know about it and how did you obtain this information, could you tell us, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I was personally acquainted with the commander of the Viktor Bubanj barracks at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And what do you know about these matters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: All the weapons in the Viktor Bubanj barracks remained in those barracks. They left with empty vehicles and with the men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of weapons are you referring to, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The weapons that were in the barracks. There were mortars, automatic rifles, sniper rifles, I think a military police battalion was there. I think it was a military police battalion barracks before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there mobile material, too, mobile equipment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Military vehicles, only lorries. There weren't any combat vehicles with weapons on them, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know, do you have any personal knowledge of the situation in other important barracks, in the part of Sarajevo which was under the control of the Presidency, and I am thinking of the Marshal barracks and other barracks in Bistrik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I haven't quite understood the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether the situation you have described in the Viktor Bubanj barracks, was the same in other barracks, for example, in the Marshal Tito barracks, in the big Marshal Tito barracks, and in Bistrik, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Firstly, that is a leading question. Secondly, he invited the witness, my learned colleague invited the witness to indicate whether he had any personal knowledge. The situation in relation to the barracks he has told us about was not personal knowledge, and so that should be made clear as well. Thank you. That is the basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in my opinion, the question is not a leading one because we know the names of the main barracks and the fact that I have named them does not lead. I don't think it is possible to make an error of any kind. As far as the issue of knowing whether the witness has any personal knowledge of these matters, obviously, we can put the question to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the question is first to establish, but I did understand that that was the question, whether the witness has any personal knowledge of -- let me put it in a neutral way -- on what happened in other barracks. No, I must say the last question, was: "Witness, do you know whether the situation you have described --" answer: "Yes." Do you have any personal knowledge of what happened in any other barracks. You told us that as far as the Viktor Bubanj, you learned that since you knew the commander. About the other barracks, what would you know about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know about the Jusuf Dzonlic barracks. I have personal knowledge about that. Because when the army left those barracks, the Patriotic League and the Green Berets, separated lorries -- the lorries often went off in three directions so the third lorry arrived in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How do you know that? So you said the lorries arrived in Nedzarici. Were you present at these barracks, the Jusuf Dzonlic barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't in the barracks, in the Jusuf Dzonlic barracks, I was in Nedzarici at the time. And I met those men who were in the lorries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps you start asking where he met these people who arrived in Nedzarici. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These persons who were in the lorry, that's what I heard, who were in the lorry, who were they and where did they come from, to clarify matters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: They were the soldiers who were in the Jusuf Dzonlic barracks after the agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will stop you there. Did you have the opportunity of personally talking to these people; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes, I was among about 10 other men when they arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you able to receive particular information from -- specific information from these persons; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So, what did these people tell you about the situation in the barracks concerned, and with regard to weaponry?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: All the heavy weapons remained in those barracks, and the personal arms which they took out were taken away from them when they were separated into four parts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do I understand that people who came to Nedzarici didn't have any weapons on them any more; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes. They didn't even have any personal weapons. They had been taken from them, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to this matter of weapons, do you know whether heavy weapons remained in the hands of the BH forces and did they remain in these barracks that you have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of heavy weapons remained there; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what kind of weapons remained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will stop you there. You used the plural. Do you know how many tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue with regard to other weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Tanks, mortars that were part of the weaponry of each barracks, and mountain cannons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said -- I don't know whether these are mountain cannons or what we call "field guns." What is the term that you used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I mentioned mountain cannons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. That's clear now. You mentioned mortars. Do you know what the calibre of the mortars that remained there was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether in addition to the, strictly speaking, military barracks, do you know whether the police barracks suffered the same fate as the two barracks that you have mentioned? And I am talking about the matter of weapons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you provide us with any specific examples? Could you give this Trial Chamber some specific examples?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Next to Sarajevo, above Bascarsija, there was a warehouse belonging to the Territorial Defence. And likewise, in the Butmir neighbourhood where the special police of Bosnia-Herzegovina had a base, they had a weapons warehouse there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you have any personal knowledge, since you were member of the Territorial Defence, do you know where the Territorial Defence kept its weapons or where it had its weapons warehouses, in general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I think the Territorial Defence had some warehouses in the -- as part of the -- within the municipality. And some large warehouses were in the territory of Sarajevo, as least as far as Sarajevo was concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "warehouses" do you know where these ware houses were located, geographically? Where they were located physically, which buildings were they located in? Which facilities were they located in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: As far as the Faletici warehouse is concerned, I don't know exactly, but the Krtelji warehouse next to the civilian airport, yes, I do know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you know if state companies were asked to play a role within the framework of the Territorial Defence and also with regard to these weapons, and if yes, what was that role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Well, just like the local communes, companies had also an organised Territorial Defence within the framework of their companies, and they also had weapons, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would now like to move on to another subject, that is, the point in time when in your military experience you moved from the Territorial Defence to the army. Could you tell us, if you can remember, as from when you yourself changed your position from the Territorial Defence to a body which became technically a military army body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: As far as I know, the structures remained the same, only the Army of Republika Srpska was established. And from the beginning, from our involvement in the Civil Defence --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will interrupt you. As from when do you consider the VRS structure to be established in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the intervention by my learned colleague. The answer was responsive to the question, and I ask that the witness be allowed to complete that answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You started answering the question that, as far as I know, the structures remained the same, only the Army of Republika Srpska was established." And then you continued, "and from the beginning, from our involvement in the Civil Defence --" could you please continue your answer at that point. So you said: "Only the Army of Republika Srpska was established" and then you said "from the beginning, from our involvement in the Civil Defence. " Would you please complete the answer you started to give there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the formation of the Army of Republika Srpska, this happened, I think, at the end of May. And then formations were set up and lists. And the period prior to that when we were in the Civil Defence was retroactively counted as military service. So it measures from that that the army was formed on the 4th of April, but in fact it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say it was an administrative measure that the army was there from the 4th of April, but in fact it was only at a later date that the Territorial Defence changed into the Army of Republika Srpska. Is that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Territorial Defence is an aspect of defence. It is a form of the military, but it is an organisation of the civilian population, you see. First of all, there was the Territorial Defence, and after the Army of Republika Srpska was established, and that was at the end of May, in my opinion, I think it was the end the May, then retroactively they recognised our service as if we had been in the army. When the army itself was being formed, it was -- people were reviewed to see what kind of military specialty they had from their years -- year of military service in the JNA, so that a proper army could be formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now focus on the point in time when you formally became a part of the VRS -- VRS structure. Can you tell us what was your company, and what were your duties. But before you answer my question --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before the witness answers, I would like him to tell us that in private session so that for shouldn't be any problem in view of the position he held.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, for the future, I would be grateful if you would not repeat your position for reasons of your own protection. But we know now what your position was. Witness, with respect to Nedzarici, could you tell us what was the extent of the destruction in that area; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe some details for us, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The destruction was considerable because we were fired at with every possible means, except airplanes. Nedzarici is a small area surrounded with high-rise buildings so that we were an easy target throughout the war. The height of the surrounding buildings was between 8 and sometimes it went up to 12 storeys.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This destruction, Witness, mainly, which weapons were used to carry it out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Multi-barrel rocket launchers, hand-held rocket launchers of foreign make, not from the arsenal of the former JNA. I mentioned already mountain cannon. There was a tank attack on Nedzarici at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: And houses were torched at the very beginning of the war because they would send Serbs who had stayed behind in Dobrinja V to run with petrol cans and they would target them. And on one occasion, one man threw away this petrol can and managed to run over to our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I am looking at the list of weapons that you mentioned. You mentioned multiple launchers, manual rocket launchers. You mentioned mountain cannon, a tank attack, incendiary devices. Was there anything else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: And every other artillery and small arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will be slightly leading, and I apologise. Were mortars never used against Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I apologise. I omitted to mention that. I simply can't remember everything contained in the whole arsenal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No problem. Could you please tell us when this tank attack against Nedzarici took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The tank attack on Nedzarici occurred at the beginning of June, the month of June, around the 10th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many tanks were involved in this attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Three tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see them yourself, and if yes, did you see them open fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I saw them with my own eyes, and I saw them fire, being opened against us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you engage them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes. We destroyed all three tanks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. After the destruction of these three tanks, do you know, yes or no, whether the enemy forces still had any such tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many tanks those forces still had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I personally know of one other tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us where this fourth tank was positioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. The question should indicate a time, at what stage did he know where the fourth tank was positioned, in other words, where was it, when?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you could ask the witness to -- ask about the basis of his knowledge. Where he says "I personally know about it," could you please ask him how he knew, and perhaps that could include a place as well, and the time might be relevant as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned a fourth tank. My first question: How do you have personal knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: It opened fire on or one of the areas of Nedzarici and the position with five shells where my brother was stationed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, when was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: In mid-1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, at that point in time what was the place from which fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Sarajevo neighbourhood called Brijesce Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us check the transcript. Maybe you will need to spell it -- no, no, it is fine. Thank you. Did this tank continue to shoot for a period of time after the date you mentioned, and if yes, until when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: In mid-1993, I went away for treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When did you get back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: When I returned, I was no longer in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have any personal knowledge through contact that you may have had about this matter, that is, whether the tank stayed on -- stayed in that position after these facts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question is contradictory. It asks for information based on personal knowledge at the time that the witness has indicated he wasn't there. Through contacts, again, it is an invitation for the witness to give hearsay evidence without any qualification as to how far it is removed from eyewitness observations

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is a bit confusing. I had a few questions in mind to clarify. When you say the place where your brother was stationed. Where was that? Was that also in Nedzarici or was that not in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Nedzarici, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. That was not clear from your answer at that moment. I didn't know where your brother was stationed. Then you told us something about -- you say you left Nedzarici mid-1993. About the activities of this tank firing, was that when you were still in Nedzarici or when you -- after you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was active while I was in Nedzarici, but it continued to do so after that because my brother told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Your brother told you that after you left that the tank continued firing. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Those were the questions that I wanted to put to the witness, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your brother, who was in Nedzarici, did you learn until when this tank remained active; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question. I appreciate your earlier ruling as to the admissibility of hearsay, and I appreciate you may say it is a question of weight, but at least I take it objection. Thank you. In other words, whatever the witness tells us will be what his brother told him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, he cannot tell us anything else on the basis of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. But at least it is important when we know that certain other witnesses told us that this tank was not functioning, that we should know what was happening in a certain area in a certain period of time. This is not distant hearsay, it is his own brother who was armed and exposed to fire at the time we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether that is the same tank or not that we heard from other witnesses, but this question may be put to the witness. So the question was whether you heard from your brother until when this tank continued to fire? Did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Until the end of 1994. And it wasn't just my brother, but I know almost all the people living in that neighbourhood. It wasn't too big. They are all neighbours. I have a large number of relatives and friends among them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we are talking about weaponry, you mentioned multiple rocket launchers. Were there several types of these rocket launchers; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us, please, the type or the types that were active in the area that you are familiar with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: These weapons did not come from the former JNA, because it had six barrels whereas the former JNA had 32 barrels, many more in any event. I am not sure of the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. How can you be certain that those weapons were used? In concrete terms, on the basis of what did you come to that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: When they fired at us in Nedzarici, when they make a hit, a part of the rocket remains and one can see what type it is. Also, it has a very specific sound as it flies through the air, as it uses rocket fuel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, could you tell us something about the frequency of these attacks on Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Are you referring just to these weapons?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, for the moment. I am just referring to these multiple rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: There were four or five such attacks, but I am talking only about the very intensive and frontal attacks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You tell us now what was the frequency of shelling? And when I use the word, "bombardment" I am referring to the use of mortars.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Until the -- until September or October 1992, these were very frequent, virtually every two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When those attacks occurred, what was the calibre used, if you were able to recognise them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: 60 millimeters, 82 millimetres, and 120 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Specifically, did the shells fall only on the defence lines or did those shells spread out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: They fell all over the Nedzarici neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you in a position to give us an explanation of the reason why these shells fell all over Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question is whether the witness is in a position to do so, to explain whether he is or he is not. So the question is not to ask him to explain, but to tell us whether he would have any specific knowledge on the basis of which he could explain that these shells fell all over Nedzarici. So I am not asking for -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin did not ask you for an explanation, but to tell you whether you had any specific knowledge or experience that would allow you to explain this phenomenon. Please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I understand that the objection has been overruled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I did overrule the objection by telling the witness exactly what your question was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what is your competence in this area? What I mean is, regarding the events of shells being -- mortar shells being fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Anyone who was in Nedzarici can explain the sound they make.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But your qualifications as a military man, did it give you more concrete experience regarding problems linked to mortars than others? And your specific qualities which I will not refer to that you had during the war, did this give you greater competence than any ordinary infantry soldier would have, for instance? Infantry soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you tell us, as far as you know, why this spread of mortars in Nedzarici -- mortar shells --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin is asking you questions about the fact as you told us that the shells would fall all over Nedzarici. What is it that gives you knowledge or expertise to explain to us why it was that these shells fell all over Nedzarici and not, for example, on certain areas or certain locations? So what would give you the knowledge or the expertise to explain why this happened? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Though I must say I don't quite understand the question, I will do my best to answer it. Because I lived through many things that I did not know about. I knew how to recognise the sound of a mortar shell when it is fired. The area of Nedzarici is very small. Factually, it could be measured in square meters not kilometres so that in my opinion it is not possible to hit exactly within a metre with a mortar. They shooting and in doing so they covered the whole area of Nedzarici when there were major infantry attacks, and this was normal fire support accompanying infantry attacks probably so that our soldiers couldn't come to our assistance who were on leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you are telling us is that on the basis of your experience and having regard to the limited area of Nedzarici, that it would be not well possible to respond to infantry attacks without hitting with these shells approximately the whole area of Nedzarici. Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that when they opened fire, they fired at the front lines, they also fired at the middle. Because these were small houses with narrow streets, and men would have to go along those streets, the men who were on leave. There weren't many soldiers in Nedzarici in a certain period of time during the war. Sometimes there would be one man at one guard post for the whole night. And when the attack start, and usually it would start at dawn, four of these men -- some of them slept in their own homes because we had no accommodation facilities -- to be able to get to us -- the Muslims would cover the whole area with fire so the man couldn't run out. You wouldn't know where the shell would fall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You very much concentrated on one part of your answer, that was, you said: "When they opened fire, they fired at the front lines. They also fired at the middle." Do I have to understand your answer to be not only the front lines were targeted, but also the middle area, and do I have to understand your answer to be that intentionally they targeted every part of Nedzarici or is this a wrong understanding of your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether it was intentionally. Or when you fire 100 or 150 shells, there may be a margin of error. I said, at least that is my opinion, that a mortar shell cannot hit the target within a metre or half a metre. And one further point, we would find the tails of mortar shells, manufactured by various countries. Now, what kind of ammunition they are, some may have a greater charges, some smaller charges. I am not an expert. If you have three shells coming from three different countries, maybe there are differences between them as to their range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you are telling us it may have been targeting errors, it may have been intentional targeting of different areas. And targeting errors were acceptable for you because on the differences on the ammunition of which you round the rest on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The remnants. All three possibilities are valid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. In view of the time, I think this is a good moment for the break, in view of the fact that when we return I need to specify something in the absence of the witness. I need to look through the transcript to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I think that we could have the witness come in now. There is only one question that I want to ask, to specify something. And during the break, we would like to ask the technical booth to be ready to show the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but before we do so -- yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Two quick matters before the witness is brought in. You may recall the Defence was required to provide us with father's name and dates of birth of the witnesses. They have provided some. We are at a point now where we only have the relevant information for about the next five witnesses. That is holding up our searches. So could we have the balance of the witnesses fairly quickly. And secondly, we don't yet have the names of the witnesses or the order of witnesses for the next seven days. I think they are in breach of that rule. I would be grateful if perhaps during the next break, Defence counsel could tell us who will be the witness for next Thursday, that is after the videolink, and who will be the witness for Monday and tomorrow. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would you please deal with that during the next break and see whether the information can be given if your -- if there would remain a problem we will see that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We will do that, gladly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then some suggestions have been made by Mr. Ierace during the first part of this morning -- of this morning's hearing. One suggestion was to receive a consolidated version of the 65 ter summary. The second one was to receive at the beginning of the testimony the sources, I would say, the documents in which to find the parts of the 65 ter summary. The Chamber has decided that if the evidence -- if the Defence gives an update on the 65 ter summary or parts of summaries that have been provided to the Prosecution before, that every such update which need not be to be in a consolidated form, although it would be very convenient. But the Defence is not required to give a consolidated 65 ter when it updates its earlier summaries or parts of the summary, but it should indicate where to find any earlier 65 ter summary or part of a summary. It goes without saying that if the Defence would decide to make a consolidated version, that it is not necessary any more to indicate the previous sources. The Chamber has carefully listened to the position Mr. Piletta-Zanin has expressed, that the Prosecution should carefully read the correspondence. It is not only for the Prosecution, it's also the Chamber receives the updates in order to find our way as well. This is, I would say, an intermediary solution. No consolidated versions necessary, but sources to be provided with the update itself. Then, the Defence is also ordered that if it is clear at a certain moment that a certain subject that is mentioned in an earlier 65 ter summary will not be part of the testimony of that witness, if on the basis of the latest interviews that becomes clear, that this should also be mentioned in an update in order to avoid that the Prosecution will unnecessarily prepare for cross-examination on that issue. So if that's clear to the Defence, it should inform the Prosecution of it. Then -- yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Defence will take this into account and we would like to thank the Trial Chamber for this. Nevertheless, we would like to the specify that in the case of the Prosecution, the Prosecution had been invited to proceed in this manner, and in particular with regard to the last information you provided. And very often we have voluminous information, a lot of information, and we don't know whether the Prosecution is going to make use of this particular information or not. At the time this was not the case. This is just a remark I wanted to make. That is all. The witness can be called now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered this issue and there is a difference which gives advantages and disadvantages between the presentation of the Prosecution case and the Defence case. The Prosecutor is under an obligation to provide written statements of the witnesses to the Defence. The Defence is not in a similar obligation. So the -- sometimes the Defence will certainly have received far more information because it has been provided with the statements of the witnesses, whereas the summaries of the testimony is, of course, a different issue. It, as I said, it gives advantages. It also gives disadvantages not to receive the written statements of the witnesses. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, will the Trial Chamber be giving some consideration to the suggestion that before each witness gives his or her evidence, the Defence indicates or I am happy to indicate what is the -- what is the date of the latest notification as to 65 ter material.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN

utterances.text: A form --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to go back to what you were telling us just before the break. When you were speaking about the shelling of the so-called Muslim part in Nedzarici and with regard to the attacks. Do you remember speaking about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I think I heard you say that this shelling, this large-scale shelling was related to what is technically and militarily termed "preparation for an infantry operation," is that what you were saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you tell us what such preparation in technical terms consists of, since you were present during these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: First of all, mortar attacks start. They fired from a gun, which was on Mojmilo. It was a B-1 mountain gun, and in four or five cases, they fired from a multiple rocket launcher, as I have said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, carry on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: They also used hand-held rocket launchers which hadn't been produced by the military industry of the former Yugoslavia. They were very strong. They had a very specific sound and they would penetrate walls. It was only once they had penetrated a wall, broken through a wall, that they would explode inside.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When would mortars be used in the course of these preparations, at which stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: That was the first fire engaged by the enemy army. They would start with mortar fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What was the purpose of such preparation? What was its objective? And when I say "objective" I am talking about the physical objective. What was the intention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Well, the intention of such preparations was to get the people removed, all the people who were there. Because when our men returned fire, we had to take shelter because of possible mistakes that might be made during a mortar attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were there any civilians who lived in the area concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: In the Nedzarici area, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when we speak about lines could you tell me what the depth of the line was, what we call the depth of the line was? And when I say "line" we are not only talking about trenches, but also the conflict zone and the technical zones right up to the command zone, which I think was established and was at the rear of the line. I think we can say this. What was the depth in the widest sense of the term? What was the depth of this line in Nedzarici? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: As I have already said, Nedzarici covers a very small territory, so everything was in the depth. And the command post was 30 metres from the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I would now like to examine another aspect of the combat which regards military instruction. utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never received orders, according to which you should be careful, not to fire on civilians; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No, you have misunderstood me, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps there is a problem of understanding. I will reformulate my question: Did you receive such instructions, such orders with regard to opening fire and with regard to civilians and civilian property?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: When I answered your first question, I was referring to civilians in Nedzarici. That's what I was thinking of. But when the Army of the Republika Srpska was formed, every 7 to 10 days orders would be received, and they said that if it was even possible to see civilians, fire shouldn't be opened on civilians. And if there was sporadic fire or provocations from the enemy, fire shouldn't be returned in order to save ammunition. But civilians and civilian objectives shouldn't be fired at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as far as this question is concerned, the question relating to opening fire, did you receive any specific orders with regard to opening fire; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Only when an attack was in course, only then would we receive the order to open fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: As my unit was composed of young men, zitelji, from Nedzarici, and since there were very few men, in the case of an intense attack, we would be the unit that would go to assist and to pull out the wounded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Witness.
