utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For one and the other of these buildings, according to your best recollection and until the end of your stay in the area, were the facades in this condition that we see them in now on the screen; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's continue with the tape and I will put my next question after that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we stop. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The building that we see in the background in the centre of the picture, what are those buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: It is Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would you agree with me Mr. -- witness, in saying that the angle of the building, the corner of the building that we see in the forefront is part of the student hostel, that is, the first building closest to Alipasino Polje?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to leading, Mr. President, on these sorts of issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, this is a contested issue. Could you please replay the latter part just for my -- to assist me to perhaps have replayed the last one minute, approximately, of the -- yes. No, further. So on from the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Forward, forward, forward. Yes. We can move fast forward until we get the first big white building. Please stop. Yes. Could we slowly now again see -- could you play the ... Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To make things quite clear, I will put the question once again to you, Witness: For both of these buildings, the condition of the facades as reproduced on this tape is indeed the condition that you were familiar with during your stay when you were under arms in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please now concentrate on the next question. From whatever position, that is, no matter from what position on the side of the Serb lines, could one see through the facades of these buildings shown on the screen, through those buildings; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as the question is interpreted into English, it refers -- it invites the witness to comment on whether you could see through the facades of the building quite shown on the screen. We see a little bit of a student hostel. We see a lot of building in Alipasino Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think there was no confusion. But the question put to you from Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whether from any position you could see through the building on the screen, I take it that Mr. Piletta-Zanin referred to the students' building and not to the building you also see on the screen now which is Alipasino Polje. But the question is about the students' buildings. Yes, whether you could see through it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We could only see the buildings of the students' hostels. We couldn't see what was happening behind them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you give us the name of the street if we are looking theoretically from Serbian positions, the street that was on the other side behind the so-called student buildings, the main boulevard, what was its name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I think it was called Ante Babica Street. I don't know what its name is now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To be more precise, from any position behind Serb lines and at any point in time, could one see through these buildings, that is, the student hostel, could one have a view of the Ante Babica Street; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I have already said no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for telling us once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we no longer need this tape, it can be removed, and we can now continue with the questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, shall we now focus on the question of destruction, particularly in the zone that you were familiar with. Could you tell us when, as far as you know, the bulk of this destruction was done in your area, to buildings in your area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Are you referring to Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the zone you were familiar with.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Throughout 1992. Later on, the intensity was much lower.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If we ask you about other zones of Sarajevo, did you have any knowledge of other zones in Sarajevo, apart from Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Before the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will now move on to another series of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we place under the ELMO -- I am sorry, Madam. The Exhibit is P3277. I think it is an exhibit that looks like this. This is just to save time. Perhaps we could place this one and exceptionally this very photograph on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think as a rule we should use the exhibit admitted into evidence and the quickest way of doing this is to give the number in advance to the Registry --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which has been asked for several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we did do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have changed registrars, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look to your right. You will see a photograph. Do you recognise the place; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The building marked with a "1" is it the building that we just saw on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes, it is, the second one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, do you see a street slightly going uphill from what we believe to be the Ante Babica Street, the street going slightly uphill to the left, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you invite the witness to point with the pointer so we are sure we are talking about the same street. Would you please do that on the right-hand side. Yes. Please point at the street you think the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite. That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, on this road that the witness has pointed to, a road to the left of the screen and going mildly uphill, could you tell us how many barricades there were on this road, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: There were three barricades, but we could see only one well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The one closest to Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's quite logical, indeed. Thank you. Could you show it to us on the photograph where these three barricades were, please, with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: One was here. The second was there, and the third was around the corner of these buildings, somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness has indicated that the first paragraph -- barricade, was slightly behind the first vehicle that we see on that road. Then in the middle and then further up again. The witness saying "around the corner" of the building that is seen to the left of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, in view of these obstacles, was it possible, and I will be very precise, to have a firing angle of -- on any spot on the Ante Babica Road from Serb lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me put the question to you once again: Are you positive about that; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes, I am positive. It couldn't be seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was it not possible to see anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Well, because there wasn't an elevated point anywhere, a point which was sufficiently elevated along the lines, along our lines. I think that in the distance you can see a building -- you can't see it here -- it was 70 to 100 metres --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you. Were you aware of what we call here in this Trial Chamber the house for the blind, blind children? Please answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I don't see it in the photograph, but it was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that you can't see it in the photograph, but did you personally know this institution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. From that site -- this is the question I am putting to you now -- was it possible to have a firing line, was it possible to fire at the place that I have indicated to you, that is to say, that Ante Babica Avenue down below, and taking into account the obstacles that we have mentioned; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No, it wasn't possible to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to move on to another photograph. It is Exhibit 3270. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you recognise this place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: These are the buildings in Vojnicko Polje which is across the road from Nedzarici. I don't know what this part here that has been scribbled over is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please ignore that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not important. It is not important. Act as if it wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to ask you a question about the buildings which in the middle of the photograph and in the background, could you indicate them with the pointer, please. Would you take the pointer, please. I don't know if the gentleman has a pointer. Yes. And could you point to it in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine. That's right. At the time that you were familiar with as a soldier, could you tell us who occupied these buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The Muslim Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove this photograph from the ELMO, and I would now like to place a map on the ELMO. It is Exhibit 1785 and concerns incident 23. It is one of the incidents that concerns Nedzarici. We are going to present this map. Would you hand this out, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just to give you an indication, if you would use two hours for this witness, that would be another 15 minutes, approximately, a bit less. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the photograph on the screen, this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I'd like you to take the pointer and point to the red triangle under the word "Nedzarici." Could you do that, please. Can you see a red triangle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. But in the red triangle, could you point within the red triangle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The witness has complied. Witness, I don't want to be too specific, but what was there within this terrain? Was this a field, an open plane, were there buildings there or I don't know what? Could you describe the terrain to us within this triangle. What did the terrain look like at the time that you were familiar with as a soldier, naturally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: We'll start from here; is that all right? In this part up to this road there were houses which were completely destroyed. There were two or three houses at the corner itself. There was a field here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness indicated the exterior part of the triangle behind the word "Nedzarici" and he said that there were buildings in this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: There was a field here. This is where the houses started. This is where there were private houses, and then there was a field here, an open field. And this was a theological faculty in Nedzarici. It started from the Mojmilo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it is important that we have an accurate description of what the witness has just said. Could you also, Mr. President, start with the portion that my learned colleague described, because it comes out in English translation as an area beneath the term "Nedzarici" which doesn't concern many --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me give it a try. The witness started explaining what is in the triangle going from -- to a red dot related to the number "23." He then told us that after the first double line, houses would start going to the left approximately to where the word "Nedzarici" is above the triangle. The part of the triangle just under the word "Nedzarici" was described as being a field. Then further to the left where the colour starts, the witness indicated that there were houses, and then the last part to the left of this triangle being without colour, the witness indicated that there was a field. And he then pointed at what seems to be a structure left of number "75" just outside the triangle and said that that was the theological faculty in Nedzarici. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have two questions that I would like to put to you. They are as follows: First of all, since this -- I don't comment on that. First of all, what is the distance between the point that you have described as the theological faculty and the point which is indicated as number "23" which is marked with number "23"? So in your opinion, what is the distance between these two points, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I think it is about 1.300 or 1.400 metres from one point to the other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Could you indicate number "23" the red point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The witness has complied with the request. Around this point that you are pointing to, were there any enemy positions, and if yes, what can you tell us about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Well, there was a cannon, more or less, near this point which fired on Nedzarici. Fully, not just where it is inscribed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there operators with that cannon, too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there an exchange of fire between the two sides, and if so, how frequently did such exchanges occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: What do you mean "between the two sides"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Serbian side and the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Along all the lines?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, in general. Yes, and more specifically in that zone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Very frequently; every two or three days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Under point "23" that you have mentioned, as far as you know, were there also military establishments, establishments of military troops?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to leading on these sorts of issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will reformulate that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Under point "23" do you know what was located there at your -- at the time that you were a soldier? I am referring to the zone in general.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Somewhere here, more or less. There was a water reservoir and before the war broke out, the JNA had positioned itself there. And about two months later, they were under fierce Muslim attack. They weren't able to return to Lukavica by this road. The combat vehicles, a tank and five armoured carriers remained there. They descended to our barracks in Nedzarici and then they came to us in Lukavica and got around. But all those weapons remained there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As a result, that position, in whose hands was that position after the attack, the position that was described as being the one where there was a water reservoir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The Muslim Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, the witness indicated the extreme point of a curving, a serpentine road which finishes just under the red point which concerns incident 23.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like the change the subject, to move on to another subject. And very briefly, what do you know about the elevated points, and I am referring to military positions of both sides. What do you know about elevated points in Sarajevo or around Sarajevo? For example, the Mojmilo hill, what do you know with regard to army positions? Who held Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The entire Mojmilo hill was under the Muslim Army. That was a dominant position above Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Who held the Zuc hill?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, perhaps first address the Prosecution. We have heard quite some testimony on who held what hills. As far as my recollection goes, this testimony was mainly concurrent. Does the Prosecution contest, I would say, the main lines of that testimony given until now about Zuc, about Trebevic, about Mojmilo, about Hum, about ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, yes there was much evidence about who held those positions at various times in the Prosecution case. As I recollected in relation to Mojmilo, one party held it earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mojmilo might be different, but especially the other before we go into all the hills again. Perhaps I should not speak about it at this very moment. Perhaps just to the parties that this --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, the Defence can tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the Defence would tell what their position in this respect is and see whether we can avoid, if not necessary, repetitious evidence on that. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is one of the items you could see on my list this morning, but I have to continue with this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same question for Zuc, do you know who held the Zuc hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Muslim Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The same question for the Hum hill.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: That was in the depth of Muslim territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- the same question for --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you allow me just one minute. I am unable to access my transcript at the moment. It will take me a few minutes. But do we have clear as to what period of time we are talking about as to when these positions were held?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us if the hills that you were questioned about during the period of the armed conflict, that the forces that were holding these hills changed, would you please then indicate. So I take it if the answer is put to you that it is for the whole period, if that would not be possible to answer the question in such a way, please indicate so. Yes. So if there was any change during the conflict. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what the situation was in the area called the Seven Woods area; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I haven't heard about the Seven Woods area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I am going to move on to another subject. Witness, have you ever heard anything about a plan that was allegedly one of your army's plans, the purpose of which was to destroy and move out from Sarajevo all property or all Muslim property, all Muslim people, have you heard about such a plan for massive destruction; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to return to the questions of symbolic objectives. In the Nedzarici area or near the Nedzarici area, were there any monuments such as mosques; yes or no? Were there any sites such as mosques?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What are you referring to and where? Which location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: In the Aerodrom, the airport neighbourhood, this is near Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As far as you know, this mosque, was it intentionally shelled or destroyed or by your forces?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to the question, Mr. President, "was it intentionally shelled or destroyed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will reformulate that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any orders, for example, an order to fire on such targets; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result, you didn't receive any orders to destroy these sites; is that how I am to understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes, you have understood that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by the way, throughout the war, do you know whether this mosque was ever destroyed; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I can't say because it can't be seen from Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to have a break in approximately five minutes. I take it that you will be able to finish by then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, willingly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, at the beginning of your testimony you said that you had been wounded. Can you tell us when you were wounded, how, by what, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: On both occasions it was in Nedzarici. On the 1st occasion it was on the 19th of June. The second time was on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you wounded by?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The first time I was wounded by a bullet, and the second time it was a hand-held rocket launcher when it hit me when I went to fetch the wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you recognisable when you went to see -- when you went to pick up the wounded? Was it possible to recognise you as someone who was trying to provide the wounded with assistance?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. Again, the question is inappropriate to the question to that issue. Might I respectfully suggest should be, what was he wearing at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that would be the proper way of putting it. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the question -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. I apologise. But if, for example, this person was wearing a camouflage uniform and a stretcher, he could have that with the Kalashnikov. But I think Mr. Ierace's objection with regard to clothing is not pertinent. I don't know if he had a stretcher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, that the objection was that you should not lead the witness in this respect and whether you would not lead him by asking about what he did wear at the time or what he had with him or how he moved around, that is all fine, but the issue is not leading. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you carrying weapons when you were wounded the second time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to continue -- no, I am going to finish with this question. Were the wounded in open territory, the wounded or the wounded, if there were several of them, were they in open terrain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I haven't understood your question. What do you mean by an open area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the terrain like? What kind of terrain were the wounded in, the wounded that you assisted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: They were in our existing positions because we always defended ourselves, we never attacked. When someone was wounded, the colleagues would take them to a secure place until we arrived because the medical unit couldn't come. My unit went to get the wounded out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a specific place where one received the wounded for your unit or was there a specific place where one collected, where one gathered the wounded; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: When the wounded would be taken away from the unit, they would be taken to the medical place which was at the barracks for a certain period of time, and then at the theological faculty and then they were taken to the hospital after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the incident, where did this incident take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: It was in the street that you have asked me about, the Aleja Branka Bujica where the old primary school used to be. I came to get the wounded, and when we were leaving, they put us in the building of the student home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. This is my very last series of questions. I would like to know whether you knew about military objectives, strategic objectives on the other side in the town of Sarajevo, and in particular, objectives such as workshops, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The people who would go out in the course of the war who were captured or who were in the Viktor Bubanj Barracks, there was a prison there, we would receive information from them. Or rather, the army, the police, military police would receive information. They gave statements according to which they had started producing in the engineering centre, in the very centre of town, where there were workshops before the war too, where they had tools of various kind, for the education of pupils. I heard that they produced then in the Vaso Miskin Crni factory. And I heard about the Zrak factory which they produced optical sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I want, Mr. President, the -- the evidence is in a very general hearsay form, and as you have required with earlier in the Defence case it should be more specific as to who said what. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. It is obvious that if we want to prove that a certain firing was justified in Sarajevo itself, it would be very difficult for us to find people on this side who were in Sarajevo itself, and also on the other side. So the only reasonable source of information is the information that military personnel had at the time. And if we can't obtain this information from people who lived with them, then nothing can be proven, and I don't think this is justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- the information until now is rather general. The witness testified on how he would have received this information. That is perhaps an area that could be further then explored because I do understand that it is not information he got from the other warring party, but from, if I may say it, his own people who have seen that at the other part. So I certainly can imagine that that is something the Defence would explore in further detail. If the witness has any -- for example, if he could tell us from whom he got this information, that might assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, and I will only have two or questions after this --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From which person, for instance, did you receive such information? Do you remember whether such-and-such a person gave you some particular information, briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I have already said that during exchanges or when Serb civilians fled that had been captured in the Federation, the normal procedure was for them to make a statement about what they knew. And this information was passed on through military channels to higher levels of command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We understood that, but do you know the names of any of those persons who gave this information, that is the question. Yes. If you would prefer to say it in closed session, then we will do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't know the name. Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the other hand, Witness, the information coming from the police went through the chain of command, is that right, was passed on along the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How many people were living in Nedzarici at the time that you were familiar with, that is 1992, 1993, how many civilians were there, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I would say around 200, 180 to 200.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And my very last question now: What do you know about the digging of trenches in the Nedzarici zone, trenches of the enemy, of the adversary, who did this and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Along the whole length of the line around Nedzarici, trenches were dug, and the digging was done exclusively by Serbs who had been captured and stayed behind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For some reason I missed the earlier question to places on the other side of the confrontation lines which might have been factories.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, I will check.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I also ask that my learned colleague, Madam Pilipovic, lower her voice. Not for the first time, I can hear her quite clearly from here, speaking in the Serbian language, which I understand to be the language of the witness. It is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do take it, Ms. Pilipovic, that it is because you have your headphones on that you sometimes do not hear yourself, that you can be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I do apologise. But this type of observation today to Ms. Pilipovic, she cannot speak. She doesn't have a voice. She is mute. That is really a bit too much. I am so sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you do not agree with Mr. Ierace. Could you tell us exactly how you know who has dug the trenches at the other side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know, because I already said at the beginning of my testimony that the sources were exclusively from the region of Dobrinja V, that the Muslim side would send Serbs with two bottles of petrol to set fire to Serbian houses. And on one occasion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I understand, you were not at that very location when people were digging trenches. You were not so close to these trenches, I take it, that you could speak with these people; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but if I may finish how we obtained that information. One man ran across to the middle of the meadow. He threw away the bottles and he ran over to the Serbian side and our soldiers --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who was that? Who was that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can give you the name of that man. But I don't know what the proper way is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will turn into closed session. We will turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say they were dug by Serbians who were captured. That is how you started your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And this man, when he arrived, he told us that it was always the Serbs who dug trenches. And usually as they were digging, they would show three fingers to the men on position -- on the front lines. Sometimes I was on guard duty and I could hear them. They were digging trenches and letting us know not to shoot at them. And we didn't shoot. And they were approaching us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they lift these three fingers, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: As a sign of recognition that they were Serbs. I doubt that a Muslim would show himself up to the waist up as digging trenches. It is rather inconceivable.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. No further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness, once he has returned in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am ready to start, and I can indicate tomorrow whether I will be ready to finish. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP5, you will now be cross-examined by counsel for the Prosecution. Mr. Ierace, please proceed. Cross-examined by Mr. Ierace:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during the questions that were asked to you by the Defence, you were shown various video clips. Do you know where those video clips came from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I think they were video clips of the Serbian radio and television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you see those video clips for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: These ones, when I arrived here at the court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had not seen that footage, that is, that video before today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Correct. This one, I hadn't seen it before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen any of that video before today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that in relation to the footage of the student hostels, therefore, you don't know where it was taken from, in other words, where the camera was positioned when it recorded that footage --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. Because the first question to be put by Mr. Ierace was whether the witness had access to this tape with sound and music or without it. So he should have started with that question, whether he had seen the tape with the sound and the music, or without the sound and music, as we viewed it, to clarify things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think the objection as such should be denied, but if that would be an issue for the Defence, perhaps it could be clarified right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the video was played to you today, we could not hear the sound track. Had you seen that video before today with a sound track?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No. I have already said, I haven't seen it at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Have the lawyers for the Defence, Madam Pilipovic, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, or any other member of the Defence team ever shown you any videotape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No. But I saw Mr. Piletta-Zanin for the first time today. I spoke to Madam Mara Pilipovic and I think his name was Voja Radovic, as investigator that came to Sarajevo two or three times. On two or three occasions they came to Sarajevo and we spoke for maybe a half hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did you first meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Whom do you mean? I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Voja Radovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Mr. Voja Radovic and Madam Mara Pilipovic came together. I think it was about eight months ago, eight or nine months ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at any stage, have you given a statement to any member of the Defence team, including investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, do you remember the part of the videotape that showed the student hostels?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever been to, during the war, the school for the blind or school for blind children, as it is sometimes known?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: On a number of occasions. Because I said that my brother was there throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't understand your evidence to be before then, that your brother was positioned at the school for blind children. Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I think I did say that when I said that the tank was firing from Brijesce Brdo, the whole of Nedzarici, including the Institute for the Blind, a position where my brother was throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying that a tank from the Bosnian government army side fired upon the school for the blind and your brother was in one of those buildings at the time; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What position did your brother have in the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, at that stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: He was an ordinary soldier throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For what period of time do you understand your brother to have been positioned somewhere in the complex of the school for blind -- school for the blind? How many weeks or months or years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: You mean in total, how much time he spent there?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: From about mid-May, that is when we entered the institute - until then there was no one there - and up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean from mid-May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is your brother still alive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want his address, but do you know where he lives?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, during -- I withdraw that. You told us you were wounded in mid-1993 and that you went somewhere for treatment. After you received your treatment, did you return to Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A problem of translation. I think I heard 1992, was it 1993? I wanted to make sure whether it was properly translated for the witness. It is okay now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go after you received your treatment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I returned to Ilidza. During my treatment, my unit, what happened was that the heavy weapons had to be placed under control so that the APCs went to the larger holes of Energoinvest in Ilidza. And the Ukrainian soldiers was in charge and I was assigned there and stayed there until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in terms of what happened in Nedzarici and your own personal observations, you can assist us up until mid-1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: For some things I can assist you after my return from treatment because I said my house was there, my brother was there, my relatives and friends who were ordinary soldiers. And when I was free, with regard to my obligations to my unit, though we weren't very busy because of the heavy weapons were under control, so I would go to Nedzarici. And towards the very end of the war, the Muslim Armies attacks were not so intensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does not mean that between mid-1993 and say September 1994 there were occasions when you went to the school for the blind children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the dates you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between mid-1993 and September 1994, did you go to the complex of buildings known as the school for blind children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: In the second half of 1993 until October 1994, I was treated at a clinic for orthopedic traumas in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that after your treatment you went to Ilidza, you were stationed with your armoured carriers where the Ukrainian brigade or battalion were, but even so you returned to Nedzarici because your brother was there and your house was there. Can you tell us, yes or no, between the time you returned from your treatment until October 1994, did you go to the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Once or twice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, having seen the video this morning of the student hostels, does it appear to you that the position of the camera was probably somewhere in the general area of the school for the blind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you went -- go on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: I apologise. The position could be from the old people's home in Nedzarici, and there were no soldiers of ours there. For a time, members of the French Battalion were accommodated there as observers at the beginning of the war to observe any violations of the ceasefire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just in relation to that, they left certainty by the end of 1992, hadn't they, the UNPROFOR soldiers from the home for old people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No. The soldiers left the old people's home sometime in October after two incidents occurred in Nedzarici. On one occasion, a French soldier was wounded --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not asking you for the information as to why they left. Do you mean October 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, whenever you visited -- on any occasion that you visited the school for the blind, between September 1992 and August of 1994, did you ever go into, up into a floor of any of the buildings above ground level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No, because it was impossible. You couldn't climb up because where the steps were, there was a glass partition that was broken, so you would be visible from almost the whole of Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the -- I understand the audio visual room has the videotape ready to show for me that I indicated to them during the break. Could I ask that the witness's monitor be switched to -- I think computer evidence gives the best picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, could you please assist. Computer evidence or video evidence? I think video evidence gives the best but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and I received something -- as a matter of fact, on computer evidence, I see there was a totally different thing. I see it is a 360 degree movie.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have noticed that the picture which we get on the courtroom monitors, for whatever reason, is not as clear as one gets when the video is watched directly on the monitor with the tape in the monitor. And that may be critical during this cross-examination, but I will persevere for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will see how things develop and whether you will be able to do. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I just wanted to check a point, but I think Mr. Ierace has already told us. I think we are talking about the video we saw a moment ago. I think that's what we are talking about, aren't we?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the screen at the moment we see what you described earlier as the remains of the Oslobodjenje building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was shelled by the Bosnian Serb Army, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes, after sniper fire. We can't see the top of this building --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask you that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. The witness was just explaining why the action took place, and I think he should be allowed to finish, as was the case earlier on during our examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you going to ask about the reasons or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not. Nevertheless, if you could just briefly finish your answer, Mr. DP5 -- no, not 5. I am making a mistake. Yes, Mr. DP5. You said "after sniper fire we can't see the top of this building," and then what would you like to add?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said that on this picture, we can't see the very top of the building. There was a rounded part from which sniper fire was opened and we had seven or eight dead. From this building, you could see the whole separation line along Lukavica Street, so that they jeopardised that line too. So we had to open fire on that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand your testimony to be that the shelling of this building took place in response to sniper fire coming from the top of that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We targeted that building the moment it was ruined. On that day, there was no fighting. There was an alarm sounded throughout Nedzarici. Nobody knew what was happening. And then a soldier saw one part of -- one wing of the building fall and then the second part. And this is the central part that we see. There were two glass parts of the building. The left part fell first, and three days later the part to the right. But we were not firing at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just -- one moment, please. One of your earlier answers was on a question about the building: "That was shelled by the Bosnian Serb army wasn't it?" You said then: "Yes, after sniper fire." How should I understand your testimony? That this destruction was the consequence of shelling or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not destruction. You didn't understand me. Always after wounding. I said that we had eight or nine killed from shots from that building. There were many more wounded. And it was only after that, if a soldier is wounded or is killed, then we would target the building to neutralise the fire coming from it. Do you understand? We had to defend ourselves. For us, it was a military target, if fire was opened from it, we couldn't just sit there and say, we don't care.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you are saying is that shelling was a response of sniper fire coming from that building, is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Perhaps we could have the image back on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the weaponry that was used to shell the building, was it tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: On two occasions, yes. But in most cases it was hand-held rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now we are talking about fire from Bosnian Serb army positions against the Oslobodjenje building. Do you understand that to be the context of my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us the collapse of the building occurred in two stages. As I understand it, the first stage immediately following shelling by tanks, the second stage part of the building collapsed a few days later; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, objection, Mr. President. That was not the testimony of the witness

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps you should ask and put that to the witness. And it is not quite clear to me whether it was his testimony or not, but please ask him, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the building was first targeted by shells, was that in particular by tanks, that is, tanks of the Bosnian Serb Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No. The first time it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: The first time they used automatic rifles, the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I am asking you about shelling, not small arms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: During the first couple of times when they opened sniper fire, our people responded with infantry weapons. Later on --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think there is a problem of translation here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. About the answer of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But actually the reply given in line 24 of the previous page was already the same as the witness is giving now. This "they" refers to the same side. I wish to underline it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please in your questions make sure that we always know for certain what part the witness is -- what party the witness is referring to. But I take it that as far as -- to listen to your answer until now, that you said, "during the first couple of times when they opened sniper fire," that you referred to BiH sniper fire, and that your people, the Serbian people, then responded with infantry weapons. And then you continued, "later on." What happened later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's what I said and I wanted to clarify this. Throughout the war what happened with this building is something that happened in November 1992. There were perhaps about 15 incidents, and it was always shelled. The first part of the building was always shelled. On that day, we didn't fire either. There were no operations. The building wasn't shelled. The first part of the building collapsed, and three days later the second part of the building collapsed. And when both parts had collapsed, well, there was no reaction. Perhaps the material failed. I don't know how to explain it. Whenever there was shelling, the Oslobodjenje building was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last part of your answer is -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it is -- the last part of your answer is: "Whenever there was shelling, the Oslobodjenje building was shelled." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I apologise. Could the witness take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will ask him to do so, but do you understand any English? Do you understand any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I saw you reading on the screen, as a matter of fact. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I ask the witness to take his headphones off, but first do not go in any detail, what would you like --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I would like to say that in the transcript something appears in the affirmative, whereas --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please take your headphones off, please. And Mr. Usher, could you please switch off the transcript, if that is on the screen. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would prefer that the witness leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then would you please ask the witness -- could you please leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I know that you have your headphones on, and I know that you can't talk, but I heard you talking, as the Chamber did before. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I just wanted to check about this with my colleague. What I wanted to say is that perhaps there is some confusion in the translation. Because the witness said "We didn't" -- he said "We didn't fire, we didn't shell." In the transcript, this may have appeared elsewhere, it was possible to understand what the witness said as being "we." Phonetically, there is a resemblance, so this may have been the cause of confusion. I asked for Ms. Pilipovic's opinion, she nodded, and I think we moved from the negative to the positive in the transcript. What the witness says in the English transcript -- in the English transcript it says "It was always shelled --" I don't have it in front of me, but that is the passage concerned. The witness had clarified this matter and I am drawing your attention to this now because we will not be able to do so later on, and during the break I have managed to cut off the blink with my computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the lines are not correct because my LiveNote is not functioning on from the beginning. I lost the first two pages. But the first question put by the Prosecution on whether the building was shelled, the answer, least as it appears in the transcript is "yes." That, as a matter of fact, what is in my recollection as well. I know now by now that "Da" means yes. Whatever the witness said later on, is it the position of the Defence that the first time the witness answered that question, he did not say yes after sniper fire; that the your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, what I said is that I did not hear the witness saying this in his own language, but I may have made a mistake because things are going very fast and I guess I recognise the fact that I made a mistake, but I did not hear what I can see in line 21, page 87 -- page 97. I didn't hear "It was always shelled." And there was something -- this is something I didn't hear the witness say. I didn't hear the witness saying that it was always shelled. But I may have made a mistake. But I wanted to draw your attention to this immediately since we are relying on the English transcript. That's all. And this is at page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do understand that you did not hear him say that it was always shelled, but Mr. Ierace is allowed to please proceed, and if the witness said that it was no shelling, at least it is not the position of the Defence that his first answer, that it was shelled in response of sniper fire, which was repeated I think on questions on my side as well. So, Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I take it that you will check this afternoon so that we know by tomorrow whether there is any --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is impossible. It is literally impossible, Mr. President, I have no access to the tape. I won't have access to the tape for four or five days. I won't have access to the Serbian tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you didn't ask me to assist you. I will certainly assist you. If you take your time this afternoon, then you will certainly get an opportunity to listen to whatever part of the tape you need. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Gladly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, when did sniping start, according to your evidence, from the Oslobodjenje building into Nedzarici? What month? What year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: At the very beginning in May or June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did sniping -- do you say that sniping continued from that building up until the time that the building collapsed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that the first response by the Bosnian Serb Army was to use infantry weapons. When was the building first shelled, and by that I mean, by artillery or tanks or rocket launchers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Never from mortars. It was never shelled from mortars because firing from mortars would have had no effect if you are after snipers. And from hand-held launchers perhaps in mid-June. And from a tank on two occasions, two shells each time because there was no time -- there wasn't time to take up position to fire at the Oslobodjenje building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You said that firing from mortars would have no effect. I take it the reason for that is that if the snipers are in a high-rise building, you really need direct fire rather than indirect fire to neutralise the sniper; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, a mortar shell even when it falls on a building, it can't completely destroy it. People remained protected inside. So that would have been senseless. What was the point?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the objective by the shelling, as you understood it, to completely destroy the building in order to neutralise the snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: No. Because we always received orders from each position from which they were firing on us. We were ordered to neutralise such fire as efficiently as possible and by causing as little damage as possible for the sake of the security of our men. And could I ask the Chamber, because it is not clear, can I draw the Oslobodjenje building? It would be a lot easier to understand then. Because those two parts were next to that middle part and they became detached. They didn't go out from the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know whether the Prosecution wants to hear more details about that. So if Mr. Ierace would like to know more, then he will certainly ask you to make a sketch. But if not, he may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that hand-held launchers were used against the building from mid-June, and then a tank on two occasions. When were those two occasions that tank rounds were fired onto the building?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think your microphone is still on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I have already said, it was in mid-June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when after that, after mid-June, were tanks -- I withdraw that. When did the building collapse, in which month or months of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: As I said, it was in November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the building next fired upon with tanks or artillery or multiple rocket launchers or a similar weapon to those after mid-June 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I want to make an objection, a formal objection, Mr. President. Could the witness perhaps take his headphones off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it is for a very simple reason. The witness always mentioned one tank. He used the singular, he never used the plural. In the transcript it says "tanks." It's in the plural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question to you was: "When was the building next fired upon with tank fire, artillery or multiple rocket launchers or similar weapons to those after mid-June 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said it was on two occasions, because that was my unit. On two occasions in June, that's when we shelled --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the second time was also in June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what weaponry did you have in your unit? Did you have -- I take it you had tanks, is that correct, a tank or tanks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: We had three Armoured Personnel Carriers, which were old, and a tank which we had captured from the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I understand you to say that it was the tank in your unit that fired on the building on two occasions in June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: Yes. I said in mid-June, and I said that the first attack with Muslim tanks was in May or the beginning of June, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was that tank ever kept at the faculty of theology?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: It was positioned, it was kept there -- I think it was there on two occasions, because once it was hit and the soldier who was in the tank, for the sake of his own security, he went to the site immediately and he was treated. And the second time was when he was bandaged, but it wasn't positioned there all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a place where it was normally positioned in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP5
utterances.text: It was located at the end of the barracks, in the last facility, 30 or 40 metres from the theological faculty. But it was within the barracks, within the compound, the barracks compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to interrupt at this point. I apologise. Yet again, as far as the first part of the answer is concerned, line 4, page 95, there is -- the opposite sense appears --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am just asking you, on page 95, I am now on line 3, so I have some difficulties in finding line 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am going to read what I have in front of me. I will read it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to leave the courtroom. We are close to a quarter to 2.00. And we will adjourn anyhow until tomorrow morning 9.00 in this courtroom. May I -- yes, please put your headphones on. We will adjourn until tomorrow, but we have to deal with one procedural issue. So I ask you to leave the courtroom accompanied by the usher, and not to speak with anyone, whoever it is, about your testimony in this court. And we would like to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.00. Yes, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, what exactly is bothering you?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What bothers me is that the witness said -- I think he said this, but again I am basing this on memory. He used the following terms, he said the tank was never there apart from on two occasions and this "never" did not appear in the transcript, so we get the contrary impression. And I don't want the witness's testimony to be erroneously interpreted at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, what I read as his answer that he says that it was there twice. That is approximately the same as never, but on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. I would like to be more precise. According to the sentence, the sentence says: "Le fait d'avoir'attempt' positionne ici signifie quelque chose en termes de position." And this means that it had some bellicose purpose, the fact that it was not positioned there. In terms of the position of the battery, that could mean something else. This is why the term "never" is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the last line of his answer, but you could check that, if you are check the tape anyhow this afternoon. The last part is: "But it wasn't positioned there all the time." Did he say that it was never positioned there, or that it was not all the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I heard the word "never" at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you find this word, the transcript will have to be corrected. So if you find the word, please write it down, and what word you heard, and then it will be -- then that specific line we will ask this to be interpreted again so that there is no misunderstanding. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will do the precise figures overnight, but I anticipate that much of the last 45 minutes of cross-examination was lost because of lengthy interventions. It impacts inevitably on the flow of cross-examination, and this is clearly a witness of some importance, as it turns out in the latter stages. I would be grateful for some guidelines before I recommence cross-examination tomorrow on interventions as to what the witness said and so on, and hopefully guidelines that would achieve fewer interventions of that nature. I say it respectfully, Mr. President, because, as I say, it does impact on the flow of cross-examination, and if that can be avoided, then I think it should. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President -- gladly. I think that you have been able to see that my interventions which concern language, let's say, are only made when it is absolutely necessary, not only for the understanding of the Prosecution, but for also of the understanding of the Trial Chamber because we only have the English transcript. And in doing this, I am trying to help everyone in the spirit of the tradition that is our tradition, in order to help justice. So this is -- if this assistance is not accepted by all the parties, well so much the worse. But I think it is my duty to do this and to try and establish the facts as clearly as possible. Last time the problem concerned the root. We have to do this. There are no other possibilities, whether this is something that the Prosecution likes or not. And I am surprised that one may think that I am using this for other reasons. I am not shocked, but I am surprised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.50 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 8th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
